You are an expert power-electronics designer synthesising the interface circuit of a
piezoelectric energy harvester. You work by experiment: you propose a circuit, it is simulated in
LTspice under several operating conditions, and you receive the measurements.

GOAL
A piezo transducer must power a sensor-node load RL from a storage capacitor at node "out".
Under EVERY operating condition below, starting from 0 V (cold start) and simulating 0.8 s:
  vout_min: vavg >= 1.8 V (settled mean output reaches the load's minimum supply)
  vout_max: vmax <= 3.6 V (output never exceeds the load's absolute maximum)
  ripple: vpp <= 0.05 V (peak-to-peak ripple in the final window)
  startup: tup <= 0.4 s (cold start: first time output reaches 1.8 V)
  settled: dv <= 0.02 V (mean output changes little between the last two windows)
Measurement windows: vavg and vpp over 0.7-0.8 s; vmax over the whole run; tup = first time
V(out) reaches 1.8 V (missing if never); dv = |mean(0.7-0.8 s) - mean(0.6-0.7 s)|.

PIEZO MODEL AND OPERATING CONDITIONS
The piezo is a sinusoidal current source Ip*sin(2*pi*f*t) in parallel with its capacitance Cp and a
20 MOhm leakage resistance, between nodes pzp and pzn (Cp = 25 nF at S1).
Its open-circuit voltage amplitude is Ip/(2*pi*f*Cp), about 3.2 V at S1; compare it with the
output window and the diode drops.
  S1: nominal; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S2: heavy load; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 150 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S3: strong excitation, light load; Ip = 100 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 2200 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S4: weak excitation; Ip = 30 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 1000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S5: low frequency; Ip = 40 uA peak, f = 80 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 470 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S6: Cp +20 %, hot; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 30 nF, RL = 330 kOhm, temperature 60 C

TEST BENCH (fixed, added automatically - do not include these)
- the piezo model between pzp and pzn; the load RL from out to 0;
- for every SYNC controller you use, a 0.5 uA supply current drawn from out (its power cost);
- a 1 GOhm resistor to 0 from pzp, pzn and every internal node (prevents floating nodes).

COMPONENTS YOU MAY USE (at most 16 components)
- R  resistor, value 1..1e+08 Ohm, nodes [a, b]
- C  capacitor, value 1e-10..4.7e-05 F, nodes [a, b]
- L  inductor, value 1e-05..0.01 H; it has series resistance 2 Ohm + 5 Ohm per mH
- D  diode, nodes [anode, cathode]: forward current flows from the first node to the second.
     Model one of DSCH, DSI, DZ33:
     DSCH = low-drop Schottky (~0.25 V at uA), DSI = silicon small-signal (~0.5 V at uA),
     DZ33 = 3.3 V zener (reverse breakdown 3.3 V, conducts ~1 uA at 3.3 V and much more above)
     Orientation matters:
       full bridge: ["pzp", "out"], ["pzn", "out"], ["0", "pzp"], ["0", "pzn"] (return diodes have
       their anode on ground);
       zener clamp on out: ["0", "out"] (cathode on out, so it is reverse-biased and breaks down at
       3.3 V). ["out", "0"] would be forward-biased and hold out near 0.7 V; it is rejected.
- S  switch, nodes [a, b], "ctrl": id of a SYNC; Ron = 2 Ohm, Roff = 1 GOhm (at most 4)
- SYNC ideal synchronous controller (no nodes, at most 2): closes its switches for "ton"
     seconds (1e-07..0.001) at the piezo voltage extrema, which occur at the zero
     crossings of the piezo current. "edges": "both" (every half period), "pos" (positive peak only)
     or "neg" (negative peak only). "phase" shifts the pulses by that fraction of the excitation
     period (-0.25..0.25). It tracks the excitation frequency automatically.
     For L-Cp inversion, ton is about pi*sqrt(L*Cp).
Nodes: "0" is ground; pzp, pzn are the piezo terminals; out is the load/storage node; name any other
nodes yourself (lower-case, e.g. n1, mid). Every node needs at least two connections, and out must
connect to the piezo through your circuit.

REFERENCE DESIGN: FBR (full-bridge rectifier, 4 x DSCH, 2.2 uF on out). Its results:

S2       1.76    1.77    20.3       -      20.7  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     ok      
S3       5.68    5.72    84.4  0.0779      14.7  ok       FAIL     FAIL     ok       FAIL    
S4       1.51    1.52    20.8       -      2.27  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     FAIL    
S5       2.26    2.28    43.5   0.318      10.9  ok       ok       ok       ok       FAIL    
S6       1.93    1.94    18.8   0.379      11.3  ok       ok       ok       ok       ok      

HOW TO WORK
- Component values are optimised automatically (an evolution strategy, up to 48 full
  evaluations per structure, running while you think), so spend your reasoning on circuit
  CONNECTIVITY (topology): which structure can meet every condition. A structure that was already
  explored is not simulated again, whatever its values.
- Each proposal is first SCREENED: with out fixed at 1.8 V, the net power it delivers is
  measured on S2, S4, S6 for its proposed values and a few automatic value presets.
  If the best preset delivers less than 50 % of the load's need (V^2/RL) on any of them,
  the design is reported back with those powers and is not tuned or simulated further.
- Each round, propose up to 3 designs with DIFFERENT connectivity (different structures, not value variants).
- Classify each design with "move": new_topology or modify_topology, and explain the expected effect
  in "rationale". Set "done": true only when you believe no further structural change can improve on
  the best design so far.
- Reply with ONE JSON object only, in this form:
{
 "proposals": [
  {
   "move": "new_topology",
   "name": "short label for this design",
   "rationale": "what you changed and why it should fix the failing checks",
   "done": false,
   "components": [
    {
     "id": "D1",
     "type": "D",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "out"
     ],
     "model": "DSCH"
    },
    {
     "id": "C1",
     "type": "C",
     "nodes": [
      "out",
      "0"
     ],
     "value": 2.2e-06
    },
    {
     "id": "L1",
     "type": "L",
     "nodes": [
      "pzp",
      "n1"
     ],
     "value": 0.0047
    },
    {
     "id": "S1",
     "type": "S",
     "nodes": [
      "n1",
      "pzn"
     ],
     "ctrl": "G1"
    },
    {
     "id": "G1",
     "type": "SYNC",
     "ton": 3.4e-05,
     "phase": 0.0,
     "edges": "both"
    }
   ]
  }
 ]
}

Round 5 of 12.

RESULTS OF YOUR PREVIOUS ROUND:

reply.reasoning:
*   Goal: Power a load $R_L$ from a piezo energy harvester.
    *   Requirements:
        *   $v_{avg} \ge 1.8\text{ V}$ (S1-S6)
        *   $v_{max} \le 3.6\text{ V}$ (S1-S6)
        *   $v_{pp} \le 0.05\text{ V}$ (S1-S6)
        *   $t_{up} \le 0.4\text{ s}$ (S1-S6)
        *   $dv \le 0.02\text{ V}$ (S1-S6)
    *   Piezo: $I_p \sin(2\pi f t)$ in parallel with $C_p$ (25nF) and 20M$\Omega$ leak.
    *   Best so far: `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener` (Score 68.16).
        *   S3 ripple: $0.061\text{ V} > 0.05\text{ V}$ (Failed)
        *   S5 settled: $0.022\text{ V} > 0.02\text{ V}$ (Failed)
        *   Other conditions passed.
    *   Second best: `SSHI_FullBridge_LCFilter` (Score 68.11).
        *   S4 startup: $0.57\text{ s} > 0.4\text{ s}$ (Failed)
        *   S3 ripple: $0.0506\text{ V} > 0.05\text{ V}$ (Failed)

    *   `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener` is very close. The failing metrics are "ripple" (S3) and "settled" (S5).
    *   S3 is "strong excitation, light load". High $I_p$ (100uA), high $R_L$ (2200k$\Omega$). This means the energy coming in is much higher than the load consumption, leading to higher voltage and potentially higher ripple if the storage capacitor isn't large enough or if the rectifier current peaks are too high.
    *   S5 is "low frequency". $f = 80\text{ Hz}$. Lower frequency typically increases ripple for a fixed capacitance.
    *   The `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener` topology consists of an L-S inductor-switch pair for flipping (SSHI) and a full-bridge rectifier.

    *   To reduce ripple ($v_{pp}$) and improve settling ($dv$), we need better filtering or better energy regulation.
    *   The `SSHI_FullBridge_LCFilter` added an LC filter at the output. This helped ripple but hurt startup time (likely because the inductor $L_2$ slows down the initial charging of $C_1$).
    *   Wait, `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener` failed S3 ripple (0.061V) and S5 settled (0.022V).
    *   Let's look at the SSHI mechanism. The current structure is:
        `L1` and `S1` act as a flipping circuit.
        `D1-D4` act as a full-bridge rectifier.
        `DZ1` clamps the output.
        `C1` filters the output.

    *   Could we improve the output filter without compromising startup?
    *   An RC filter would cause a voltage drop, which is bad for $v_{avg}$.
    *   A larger $C_1$ would reduce ripple, but might increase $t_{up}$ (though $t_{up}$ is currently ok in `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener`).
    *   Wait, in `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener`, the $C_1$ value was $933\text{ nF}$.
    *   If we increase $C_1$, ripple $v_{pp} \approx I_{load} \cdot \Delta t / C_1$. For S3, $I_{load}$ is small (2.2M$\Omega$), but $V$ is high (~3.4V), so $I_{load} \approx 1.5\text{ uA}$. $v_{pp}$ is likely dominated by the charging pulses from the SSHI.

    *   Wait, let's look at the `SSHI_FullBridge_LCFilter` again. It used $L_2 = 436\text{ uH}$ and $C_1 = 1.3\text{ uF}$. S4 startup was $0.57\text{ s}$. S4 is "weak excitation". The energy is barely enough to reach 1.8V. The inductor $L_2$ in the LC filter limits the peak current during the charging phase, slowing down the startup.

    *   What if we use a different rectification/filtering method?
    *   Maybe a Synchronous Electric Charge Extraction (SECE) or a variation?
    *   Standard SSHI (Synchronous Switch Harvesting on Inductor) usually uses a flipping switch and a rectifier. The provided "FullBridge" SSHI is basically: Piezo $\to$ L-S flip $\to$ Bridge Rectifier $\to$ $C_{out}$.

    *   To fix S3 ripple and S5 settled:
        *   S3: Strong excitation, light load $\to$ high voltage $\to$ ripple.
        *   S5: Low frequency $\to$ ripple.
    *   Both are ripple/stability issues. Increasing $C_1$ is the simplest way, but the tuner already tried to optimize $C_1$. Maybe the topology is limiting the tuner?
    *   In `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener`, the tuner chose $C_1 = 933\text{ nF}$. If we increase $C_1$ too much, $t_{up}$ might fail.
    *   What if we use a "Voltage Doubler" or "Charge Pump" combined with SSHI?
    *   The `SSHI_Doubler_Zener` failed the screen. Let's re-evaluate that.

    *   Let's try a "Parallel SSHI" or a different way to handle the rectifier.
    *   Another option: instead of a full bridge, use a half-bridge with a flying capacitor (like a Dickson charge pump) but driven by the SSHI.

    *   Let's try to improve the `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener` by adding a small series resistance or a different capacitor arrangement to dampen the S5 oscillation/settling. Actually, a better idea might be to use a slightly different SSHI structure.

    *   Wait, let's look at the $v_{pp}$ requirement: 0.05V. This is quite strict.
    *   In `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener`, the failing S3 ripple is 0.061V.
    *   In `SSHI_FullBridge_LCFilter`, the S3 ripple is 0.0506V. Almost there. But S4 startup failed.

    *   Could we use a different L-S configuration?
    *   Current L-S flip: `L1` from `pzp` to `n1`, `S1` from `n1` to `pzn`.
    *   This flips the voltage across the piezo.

    *   What if we use a "Synchronous Rectifier" instead of a diode bridge?
    *   The prompt allows up to 4 switches.
    *   Current SSHI use 1 switch for flipping. We have 3 switches left.
    *   We could replace the diodes of the bridge with switches. However, the SYNC controller only provides pulses at the extrema. A full synchronous rectifier needs a more complex controller.
    *   The SYNC controller closes switches for `ton` seconds at the piezo voltage extrema.
    *   If we use `edges: "both"`, the switch is closed at both positive and negative peaks.
    *   If we use `edges: "pos"`, it's only at the positive peak.

    *   Let's try a topology called "SSHI with Parallel Capacitor" or a different output stage.
    *   Actually, if `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener` is only failing ripple and settled, maybe we can improve the output filter without using a large inductor.
    *   What if we use a "Capacitive-Inductive" filter? (Basically a $\pi$-filter).
    *   `Rectifier` $\to$ `C_filter1` $\to$ `L_filter` $\to$ `C_out`.
    *   This might be too many components. (Max 16).
    *   Components in `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener`: L1, S1, G1, D1, D2, D3, D4, DZ1, C1 (9 components). We have plenty of room.

    *   Let's try an LC filter but with a smaller L to keep startup time fast.
    *   Wait, `SSHI_FullBridge_LCFilter` failed S4 startup at $0.57\text{ s}$ with $L_2 = 436\text{ uH}$.
    *   If we reduce $L_2$ to, say, $100\text{ uH}$, the startup will be faster, but ripple might increase.
    *   But we can increase $C_1$ to compensate for the ripple.

    *   Let's propose a design that combines the SSHI flipping and a more robust output filter.
    *   Wait, let's try a different SSHI variant: the "Parallel-SSHI" (P-SSHI).
    *   P-SSHI uses an inductor and a switch to flip the voltage of a *buffer capacitor* rather than the piezo itself.
    *   Actually, let's try a "Pseudo-synchronous" approach or just refine the LC filter.
    *   If the `SSHI_FullBridge_LCFilter` is the one to refine, how to fix S4 startup?
    *   S4 is weak excitation (30uA). The energy per cycle is low.
    *   The inductor $L_2$ in the LC filter blocks the high-frequency current spikes from the bridge, which is good for ripple, but it also slows down the average current delivery if the peak currents are what's driving the charging.
    *   Actually, an LC filter is $V_{out} = V_{rect} - L \frac{di}{dt}$.
    *   Maybe a "bypass" for the inductor during startup? (Too complex, no way to detect startup).

    *   Let's reconsider the `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener`.
    *   S3 ripple (0.061V) and S5 settled (0.022V).
    *   S5 is 80Hz. The time between pulses is longer.
    *   The "settled" metric $dv = |mean(0.7-0.8) - mean(0.6-0.7)|$ fails if the voltage is still drifting.
    *   In S5, the drift is $0.022\text{ V}$ over $0.1\text{ s}$. This means the capacitor $C_1$ is still charging slowly.
    *   If we *decrease* $C_1$, it will reach steady state faster (improving $dv$), but the ripple ($v_{pp}$) will increase.
    *   If we *increase* $C_1$, the ripple will decrease, but the settling time will increase (worsening $dv$).
    *   This is a classic trade-off. To break this trade-off, we need a more efficient way to deliver energy or a better filter (like LC).

    *   Let's look at the LC filter again.
    *   `SSHI_FullBridge_LCFilter` S4 startup: $0.57\text{ s}$.
    *   The inductor $L_2$ was $436\text{ uH}$.
    *   If we use a smaller $L_2$ and a larger $C_1$, we might get the best of both worlds.
    *   But the tuner already tried that? The `SSHI_FullBridge_LCFilter` was only evaluated 8/48 times. It might not have found the optimal $L_2, C_1$ yet.
    *   Wait, the `SSHI_FullBridge_LCFilter` had $L_1 = 10\text{ mH}$. That's quite large.
    *   Let's try a modified LC filter:
        1. SSHI flip (L1, S1)
        2. Full Bridge (D1-D4)
        3. LC filter (L2, C1)
        4. Zener clamp (DZ1)
    *   Wait, this is exactly what `SSHI_FullBridge_LCFilter` was.
    *   Let's try a different topology: "SSHI with a charge-pump" or "SSHI with a voltage doubler".
    *   The `SSHI_Doubler_Zener` failed the screen. Why?
        `L1 L pzp n_flip 0.0047`
        `S1 S n_flip pzn ctrl=G1`
        `D1 D pzp n_pump DSCH`
        `C_pump C n_pump 0 1e-07`
        `D2 D n_pump out DSCH`
        `D3 D pzn out DSCH`
        `C1 C out 0 2.2e-06`
        This is not a standard SSHI doubler. It's a bit weird.

    *   Let's try a simpler but more robust topology: **Synchronous Switch Harvesting on Inductor (SSHI) with a capacitive voltage doubler** instead of a bridge.
    *   Wait, the most reliable way to get low ripple and fast startup is a well-tuned SSHI with a large capacitor, but as we saw, that's a trade-off.

    *   What if we use a "Half-Bridge" with a "Flying Capacitor" (Synchronous Electric Charge Extraction - SECE)?
    *   SECE:
        `S1` connects `pzp` to `C_fly` (charging $C_{fly}$ to $V_{pzp}$).
        `S2` connects `C_fly` to `out` (transferring charge).
    *   This is very efficient and can have low ripple.
    *   Let's try a SECE-like structure:
        `S1` (ctrl=G1) nodes `pzp` and `n_fly`
        `S2` (ctrl=G2) nodes `n_fly` and `out`
        `C_fly` nodes `n_fly` and `0`
        `G1`: `edges: "pos"`, `phase: 0`
        `G2`: `edges: "pos"`, `phase: 0.1` (delayed pulse)
        This doesn't use an inductor.
        But we have the `SYNC` controller, which can do this.

    *   Wait, the `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener` is so close. Let's try to modify it to be more stable.
    *   What if we use a "Zener-limited" SSHI where the Zener is not just a clamp but part of the regulation? No, that's not possible with a simple Zener.

    *   Let's try a "Dual-Inductor" SSHI? No, too many components.
    *   How about an "L-C-L" filter? No.

    *   Let's try a "SSHI with a different rectifier":
        Instead of a full bridge, use a half-bridge (D1, D2) and a center-tapped-like arrangement? No, the piezo is a 2-terminal device.

    *   Let's go back to the `SSHI_FullBridge_LCFilter` and try to improve it.
    *   The failure was S4 startup ($0.57\text{ s}$) and S3 ripple ($0.0506\text{ V}$).
    *   If we make the inductor $L_2$ smaller, S4 startup improves.
    *   If we make $C_1$ larger, S3 ripple improves.
    *   The tuner should be able to find this. The reason it failed might be the $L_1$ value or the $t_{on}$ of the flipping switch.

    *   Let's try a different approach: **The "Parallel-SSHI" (P-SSHI)**.
    *   P-SSHI:
        The inductor $L$ and switch $S$ are in parallel with the piezo.
        Wait, the standard SSHI *already* does that. $L$ and $S$ are used to flip the piezo voltage.

    *   Wait, look at the `SSHI_FullBridge_Zener` results again:
        S1: $V_{avg}=3.02\text{ V}$
        S2: $V_{avg}=2.09\text{ V}$
        S3: $V_{avg}=3.38\text{ V}$, $V_{pp}=61.5\text{ mV}$
        S4: $V_{avg}=2.31\text{ V}$
        S5: $V_{avg}=3.14\text{ V}$, $dv=0.022\text{ V}$
        S6: $V_{avg}=2.46\text{ V}$
        All are very good, except S3 ripple and S5 settled.

    *   Could we add a small capacitor in parallel with the piezo ($C_{extra}$)?
        No, that would just increase $C_p$, which reduces the voltage gain of SSHI.

    *   What if we use a **Synchronous Rectifier** for the bridge?
        The SYNC controller can't do the 4-switch bridge timing.

    *   Let's try a **"Voltage-Doubler" SSHI** (correctly implemented):
